text.2_Chapter, 3_Tosefta: A child that was holding onto the hand of his father or that was riding on his father's shoulders: [When there is] a doubt regarding his [purity status], he is deemed impure, because his father is inquired of on his behalf. A deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor: [When there is] a doubt regarding their [purity status], they are deemed pure, because they do not have the mental capacity for inquiry. Said Rabbi Shimon: In regard to this [halacha], the logic is deficient.
text.2_Chapter, 6_Tosefta: An infant that is found standing next to a block of hardened dough*see Jastrow (כופת), or next to a jar of liquid, Rabbi Meir renders it pure and the Sages render it impure, for the nature of a child is to slap [his hand at the dough or the jar] (Mishnah Tahorot 3:7). Rabbi Yosei says, if he could reach out his hand and touch it, it is impure, and if not, it is pure. Furthermore, Rabbi Yosei says, [if the infant] is found far from the started dough*עיסה (an earlier stage in the doughmaking process than "hardened (or risen) dough" (בצק)), even though the hardened dough is in his hand, it is pure, for I could say, another [person] took [the hardened dough] and gave it to him, but if he said, "It is clear to me that no one came here*שלא בא אדם לכאן (MS Vienna; GR"A)," it is impure. Rabbi Ilai said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov*not "Rabbi Eliezer ben Yosei" (GR"A), in regards to a dog, behold, it is pure, for he can say, liquid is always to be found (i.e., is readily accessible), but food is not always to be found.
